For temporary NextItNet faults, ensure the inference wrapper calls the actual mutated model: register it as a child module and route wrapper.forward through its log2feats/predict_score methods; avoid closures referencing another instance or cached features. Call modules as module(x), since direct .forward(x) bypasses their hooks. functional_call substitutes parameters/buffers, not dilation, padding, or arbitrary Python attributes; pass cloned tensors because in-place operations can mutate supplied dictionaries. Verify execution with a hook counter and a controlled perturbation. [Module documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Module.html), [functional_call](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.func.functional_call.html).

For causal Conv1d, dilation changes require matching left padding, (kernel_size−1)×dilation, and consistent cropping to preserve sequence length and causality. Inspect whether padding lives in the convolution, explicit F.pad, or wrapper attributes; nonzero padding modes also use cached padding metadata. Recommended implementation: an exception-safe context manager that snapshots every altered attribute, parameter/buffer values, per-module training flags, and hook handles; restores them in finally; removes only newly installed hooks; and preserves existing hooks. always_call=True can run hooks after forward exceptions, but does not replace guaranteed cleanup. [Convolution implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/conv.py), [hook documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Module.html).

Preserve CPU/CUDA RNG with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[device_index]); separately save Python, NumPy, and custom-generator states when used. After both successful and deliberately failing probes, rerun fixed-input clean inference under identical evaluation/RNG conditions and compare outputs, attributes, hooks, buffers, and flags. state_dict equality alone misses ordinary attributes, hooks, training flags, RNG, and nonpersistent buffers; its shallow tensor references also require cloning for valid snapshots. [RNG documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/random.html), [state_dict documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Module.html).
